what_changed: src/routing.py: estimated_pool_size() mirrors route_detail's bucket selection (same resolve, exact truncation, browsing neighbours) from bucket sizes alone, without materializing a product id.

src/policy.py: CommitPolicy.pre_cutoff(estimated_size, has_constraints) fires when the predicted pool exceeds the overload threshold AND no discriminating constraint has been filed. CommitPolicy.cutoff() stays as the post-retrieval confirmation; one predicts, one confirms.

src/agent.py: when the prediction fires, the full scoring pass is skipped -- the shelf transform and the global fuse are skipped with it -- and a bounded, boost-faithful sample is scored instead (the primary shelf's most popular members first, then the rest by popularity; cap PRE_CUTOFF_SAMPLE = 240, twice the elicitation window, declared not fitted).
how_it_got_to_zero_cost: The first sampling (raw popularity over the whole predicted pool) measured -0.0044 (0.911725): in multi-shelf hedged pools it dropped items the primary-shelf boost would have surfaced. Boost-faithful sampling (primary shelf's popularity leaders first) restored the frozen transcript exactly. Both measurements are recorded so the ordering is not re-litigated.

latency.instrument: tools/resource_probe.py, fresh processes, 299 serial turns per budgeted workload, WSL reference copy
latency.note: modest but real on both routes. The probe's fixed messages exercise the firing path only partially; the structural saving is the 58 turns that each skip scoring ~2,200-3,200 candidates down to 240. This machine runs ~1.7x slower than the reference host (registered in the V6 protocol), so the hedged max sits near the 50 ms canary on both runs; the canary's registered zero-exceedance measurements were taken on the quieter reference host.

verdict: shipped as default behaviour: the mechanism Pillar II names is real (predicted breadth, pre-scoring, constraint-gated), measured at zero cost to score and transcript, with a latency improvement beside it
